'''UR-1060''' was a [[Star/Legends|star]] located within the [[UR-1060 system/Legends|UR-1060 system]].<ref name="TEA" /> It lay within the [[Outer Moddell systems]] area of the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell subsector]],<ref name="EAOC" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC" />

UR-1060 was a member of a quintet of stars, also including [[UR-2650/Legends|UR-2650]], [[UR-3741/Legends|UR-3741]], [[UR-8827/Legends|UR-8827]], and [[UR-9353/Legends|UR-9353]], that lay at the outer edges of the [[Monsua Nebula/Legends|Monsua Nebula]].<ref name="TEA" /> Those stars were much [[Time/Legends|older]] than the young [[Blue giant/Legends|blue giants]] and [[Brown dwarf/Legends|brown dwarfs]] located at the center of the [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]], and they were [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by several [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. Slow [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] and local interstellar anomalies made the stars inaccessible to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]]<ref name="Endor" /> despite [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]]-long attempts at exploration.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
UR-1060 was first mentioned in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was authored by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Jason Fry]], and was published in [[Star Wars Gamer 9|''Star Wars Gamer'' 9]]<ref name="Endor" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the star in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
